_readme: Every rule says how it is enforced. gate = a machine blocks it; scheduled = a job checks it on a timer; advisory = discipline only (say so honestly). gate and scheduled rules name the file that enforces them and a marker string that must appear in it; scripts/rules_check.py fails when an enforcer or its marker disappears. Rules start as advisory and move up only after you've wired the check into a hook, cron job, or CI (see each rule's note).

rules.rule: A task cannot close without an ack and the five-item definition of done
rules.note: dispatch.py done refuses on its own. Editing DISPATCH.json by hand gets around it, so review ledger diffs.

rules.rule: Tasks are acknowledged within 24 hours and finished by their due date
rules.note: Move to scheduled, enforced_by scripts/dispatch.py, marker 'not acknowledged after', once dispatch.py overdue runs on a timer.

rules.rule: Every agent session keeps a handoff record with all seven sections, updated after each key step
rules.note: Move to gate, enforced_by scripts/handoff_check.py, marker 'SECTIONS', once handoff_check.py --record runs in each session's stop hook.

rules.rule: Only the reconciler decides whether a delivery arrived
rules.note: Move to scheduled, enforced_by scripts/reconcile.py, marker 'def judge', once reconcile.py runs on a timer outside your AI account.

rules.rule: At 90% of the weekly quota, stop starting new work; keep only what protects scheduled deliveries
rules.note: Needs a pre-tool hook that reads your usage; see playbook chapter 6.
